family.schneider-euro-xt.description: Three approaches to bringing PC/XT compatibility home: an integrated keyboard, a revision with more memory and a desktop with a hard disk.
family.schneider-euro-xt.history: Schneider launched EuroPC in 1988 as a compact home computer supplied with a monitor and software. EuroPC II retained the integrated keyboard format with a different motherboard; EuroXT moved the concept into a separate case with an internal hard disk. The service manual covers all three but identifies different parts and boards. They belong to Schneider's own range, with no demonstrated equivalence to the PC1512 or PC1640 previously sold under that brand.
